Exactly two hind legs descend from the rear torso and meet the dusty ground, readable at native and thumbnail scales.
Native pixels show wing roots occupying the shoulder forelimb positions and no additional front-leg pair.
The creature reads as two wings plus two hind legs with no four-legged dragon or extra-limbed substitute at either scale.
The neck cluster rises from one grounded torso with one shared limb and tail system, clearly legible in the thumbnail.
Four neck paths can be followed from the shared shoulder mass to four heads at both scales, exceeding the three-neck minimum.
At native scale, the lower necks overlap and merge into a dark central shoulder mass; four separate non-merged roots cannot be verified unambiguously.
Four heads keep separate outlines, visible jaws, and differing left, forward, upper-right, and lower-right orientations at both scales.
A single substantial torso and grounded limb system prevent the creature from reading as a loose snake bundle, duplicated bodies, head halo, or three-headed dog.
